sections.h2: What are the options for selling a house in Toms River?
sections.html:
Toms River owners can list with an agent, sell privately, or take an as-is offer from a buyer who pays cash. Which one fits depends on the house, the calendar and how much repair work you are willing to finance before closing.

The township is large and varied, with mainland neighborhoods, bayfront streets and barrier-island blocks, so a house in Silverton does not sell the same way as one in West Dover or Ortley Beach. A listing exposes the property to the most buyers and sets the price by comparison with nearby sales. A direct sale is quicker and generally leaves repairs and the township paperwork to the buyer's side of the table.

sections.h2: Where is Toms River and how big is it?
sections.html:
Toms River is the seat of Ocean County, 70 miles south of New York City and 55 miles east of Philadelphia. The township covers 52.89 square miles, of which 40.55 are land and 12.34 are water, or 23.32%. Its 95,438 residents in 2020 made it the eighth most populous municipality in New Jersey. It borders Berkeley Township, Brick, Island Heights, Jackson, Lakewood, Lavallette, Manchester, Seaside Heights and South Toms River.

Most of the township is on the mainland, where the census-designated place of Toms River held 92,830 people in 2020. Two more areas, Dover Beaches North (1,277 residents) and Dover Beaches South (1,331), sit on the Barnegat Peninsula, the narrow barrier strip between Barnegat Bay and the Atlantic. Ortley Beach, in Dover Beaches South, shares the 08751 ZIP code with Seaside Heights. Mainland addresses use ZIP codes 08753, 08754, 08755, 08756, 08757 and 08739.

sections.h2: How did Dover Township become Toms River?
sections.html:
A royal charter created Dover Township on March 1, 1768, and the 1798 Township Act made it one of New Jersey's original townships. Ocean County was formed in 1850 and made the village of Toms River its county seat. Over the next century, land was carved off to create Jackson, Brick, Manchester, Berkeley, Island Heights, Lavallette and Seaside Heights.

Because the Postal Service used Toms River addresses for the whole mainland, residents and outsiders increasingly called all of Dover Township by that name. Voters approved a name change in the November 7, 2006 referendum, with more than 60% in favor, and the township officially became Toms River on November 14, 2006. Older deeds, title records and tax documents may still say Dover Township, so ask your title company to confirm that the legal description matches the property.

sections.h2: How did Superstorm Sandy and flooding affect Toms River homes?
sections.html:
The October 2012 storm caused the township's worst flooding on record in low-lying areas, including Silverton and the downtown area, as the surge pushed Barnegat Bay up and down the shore. The barrier-island neighborhoods suffered even more severe damage. A mainland or barrier house that was flooded, raised or rebuilt after that storm carries paperwork that buyers and their lenders will want to see.

  • Elevation certificate and flood insurance history, if the address is in a mapped flood zone
  • Construction permits and the final Certificate of Occupancy for any raising or rebuilding
  • Records of repairs to utilities and heating equipment

The climate is humid subtropical, with about 49.8 inches of rain a year and roughly 24 inches of snow. Roof age, gutters and basement or crawlspace moisture are the items a buyer's inspector checks first. Buyers sometimes ask about the former chemical plant site, which the EPA designated a Superfund site in 1983; the plant stopped operating in 1996, and the township's water system has been under state-leading testing since then, according to the encyclopedia entry on Toms River. Keep a current water test on hand if you have a private well.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show for Toms River?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 100,899 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 5.7% from the April 2020 base. There are 38,047 households, 82.1% of them owner-occupied, and the median home is valued at $416,700. Median gross rent is $1,726 and median household income is $99,547, lower than the incomes in South Brunswick or Teaneck. About 21.0% of residents are 65 or older and 21.7% are under 18. Workers commute an average of 30.2 minutes. Source: Census Bureau QuickFacts.

Retail sales per capita were $34,368 in 2022, a sign of the Hooper Avenue and Route 37 shopping corridors, which include the Ocean County Mall, the only enclosed mall in the county.

sections.h2: What do rental owners in Toms River have to file?
sections.html:
Many Toms River sellers have run a rental, either a year-round tenant or a seasonal unit near the beach. The Division of Property Maintenance's rental packet sets the rules, and the fees are modest compared with the cost of fixing a failed inspection.

ItemRequirement in the township packet
Inspection fee$150 per unit
Failed re-inspection$50
Amended registration$50
Year-round rental certificateValid three years from January 1 of the year issued; new inspection on a change of occupancy or ownership
Seasonal or short-term rental on the barrier islandValid April 1 through November 30; not permitted outside that window
Scheduling noticeAt least 5 days, or 10 days from May 1 to July 15

Source: Toms River Rental Inspection Guidelines, revised October 2024. Applications go through the township's online portal and must be complete.

sections.h2: What documents does a Toms River rental inspection need?
sections.html:
The packet lists the following, and the same paperwork is useful to hand a buyer who plans to keep the tenants.

  • A certificate of insurance, registered each year under state law
  • A heat certificate from a licensed professional for fuel-burning heat sources, except for seasonal barrier-island rentals
  • Proof of ownership if the property was bought within the last 6 months or the owner does not match the tax record
  • A lead-safe certificate for any one-, two- or multi-family rental built before 1978, except seasonal rentals under six months
  • An Ocean County Health Department water analysis certificate, if the house has a well

Smoke alarm rules depend on the age of the house. Homes built before 1984 need 10-year sealed battery alarms on each level, homes from 1984 to 1990 need interconnected hard-wired alarms with battery backup, and homes from 1991 on need them in every bedroom, outside the sleeping rooms and on every level including the basement. Carbon monoxide alarms go within 10 feet of sleeping areas where a home has fuel-burning appliances or an attached garage. The township's property maintenance office can be reached at 732-341-1000, extension 8440.

sections.h2: Does Toms River require an inspection when an owner-occupied house is sold?
sections.html: Ask the township's construction and property maintenance offices whether a resale certificate or inspection applies to your address before you sign a contract. The township's building page walks through permits and final certificates of occupancy for new homes and raised homes, and any open permit should be closed out before listing. The clerk's forms page also lists an Application for No Knock and an Affirmative Statement to Receive Real Estate Solicitations, so ask the Municipal Clerk how those forms work if you have been contacted by buyers you did not invite.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and bus lines serve Toms River?
sections.html:
Toms River Regional Schools is the largest suburban district in New Jersey, with 18 schools and 14,654 students in 2023-24. It also serves Beachwood, Pine Beach and South Toms River. Students attend Toms River High School East, North or South, and the district has three intermediate schools for grades 6 to 8. Ocean County College is on Hooper Avenue, and Donovan Catholic High School is the county's only Catholic high school. Community Medical Center has 587 beds and became a teaching hospital in 2021.

The Garden State Parkway and U.S. 9 pass through, along with Routes 35, 37, 70 and 166. Route 37 is the main road from Parkway Exit 82 to the shore, and Hooper Avenue (County Route 549) is among the most congested roads. NJ Transit buses 67, 137, 319 and 559 serve the downtown station off Exit 81, where a Park and Ride has express service toward New York City at rush hour. The nearest train station is at Bay Head.

sections.h2: What state forms and fees come with a Toms River closing?
sections.html: New Jersey charges the seller a Realty Transfer Fee when the deed is recorded, based on the price in the deed, with exemptions listed by the Division of Taxation on its realty transfer fee page. A price over $1,000,000 adds a graduated percent fee. A seller who has moved out of state prepays estimated Gross Income Tax at closing, never less than 2% of the sale price, under the GIT/REP rules. Ask your closing attorney to run the numbers early.

faqs.q: Is Toms River the same place as Dover Township?
faqs.a: Yes. Dover Township became Toms River Township by a voter-approved name change that took effect November 14, 2006. Old deeds and tax records may still use the Dover name.

faqs.q: How much does a Toms River rental inspection cost?
faqs.a: The township packet lists $150 for each unit, $50 for a failed re-inspection and $50 to amend a registration. The fees are non-refundable.

faqs.q: Are seasonal rentals allowed all year in Toms River?
faqs.a: No. Barrier-island seasonal and short-term rental certificates run from April 1 through November 30, and such rentals are not permitted outside that period.

faqs.q: Do I need a lead-safe certificate to sell?
faqs.a: The packet requires it for rentals built before 1978, with an exception for seasonal rentals under six months. Ask the township and your attorney whether anything applies to an owner-occupied sale.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Toms River?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $416,700 as the median value of owner-occupied housing units for 2020 to 2024. Your own house may sit well above or below that depending on its location, condition and flood exposure.
